name: External Control of File Name or Path
principle: The program lets external input control a filename or path used in a filesystem operation. This can make the application read, write, delete, or execute unexpected files with the application's privileges.
detection_signals: Tainted input from `argv`, `getenv()`, `request.getParameter()`, headers, config, or `System.getProperty()` flows into a path variable.
Path built with `base + userInput`, `String.format(...)`, `sprintf(...)`, `Path.resolve(userInput)`, `new File(userInput)`, or `Paths.get(userInput)`.
No fixed ID-to-filename map, enum switch, or constant lookup is used before the filesystem sink.
Validation uses denylist filtering such as `replace("../", "")`, `replace("/", "")`, `replace("\\", "")`, or regex blocking only selected characters.
Code checks `startsWith(base)` or prefix equality on a raw/non-canonical path before opening.
Path value is read from writable config, environment variable, cookie, or request parameter and trusted as a filesystem target.
negative_signals: External value is mapped through a fixed ID-to-filename table and unknown IDs are rejected.
Candidate path is canonicalized with `realpath()`, `File.getCanonicalPath()`, or `Path.toRealPath()` and checked under a canonical trusted base directory before use.
Filename allowlist rejects path separators, traversal segments, extra dots, unexpected charset, and unexpected extensions.
Only compile-time constants or server-owned constants reach the filesystem sink.
OS sandbox, chroot, AppArmor, container mount, or least-privilege file permissions prevent access outside the allowed directory.
false_defense_traps: Removing only `../` or `/`; alternate separators, encodings, or repeated normalization can bypass it.
Checking `startsWith(base)` on an unnormalized string; `base/../secret` or `base_evil` can pass.
Client-side filename validation only; the server still accepts modified path values.
Regex denylist misses `\`, `%2f`, `%5c`, double encoding, Unicode separators, or absolute paths.
Canonicalizing before a later path change or symlink swap without safe open semantics.
verification_focus: Can attacker-controlled data reach a filesystem path/name sink without fixed mapping, strict allowlist validation, and canonicalization under a trusted root?

consequence_chains.trigger: User-controlled path contains traversal or absolute path syntax and is used in a filesystem operation.
consequence_chains.consequence: Files outside the intended directory are read, modified, or deleted.

consequence_chains.trigger: Aliases, symlinks, short names, or alternate path forms are not resolved consistently before the access check.
consequence_chains.consequence: The operation targets a different file than the checked file, bypassing restrictions.

patch_principle: Replace free-form path input with fixed ID-to-filename mappings and reject unknown IDs.
Apply strict allowlist validation for filenames: limited charset, no separators, single dot, approved extension.
Canonicalize the candidate path and verify it remains under a canonical trusted base directory before opening.
Use least-privilege OS permissions and sandboxing to limit filesystem impact.
